A minifying implementation emits characters directly; a pretty-printing variant can subclass/replace it, overriding these hooks to emit indentation and newlines (e.g., fixed four-space indent), while reusing the shared string-escaping logic (256-byte needs_escaping lookup table with an 8-at-a-time fast scan) and fast integer/double number formatting (fast_itoa, to_chars)."},{"read_ids":["bad5e696c19e760bc2994387aa10a673071a075fdd7284cb7198355edc845004"],"text":"Key design point: pretty printing can be added without duplicating the DOM traversal or escaping logic by parameterizing the output behavior behind the formatter interface — the traversal emits structural events, and only the formatter's open/close/comma/key hooks need to insert whitespace and indentation."}],"join_sha256":"f87dfebd659ec6e6c4f406bed364d03f972a4d6d8a30b50ed8376f2227497dbe","posture":"provisional-model-claims"},{"branch_id":"q2","claims":[{"read_ids":["80bef52853e059661a2ae91ad8c388a63291edfc735227469acd890e8143246c"],"text":"Existing documentation convention: doc/dom.md documents output-to-strings functionality (minified string via C++ stream idiom `out << element` and `simdjson::minify(element)`) under a feature bullet; The core algorithm is a formatter class (mini_formatter) with virtual-style callback hooks for each JSON event — start_array/end_array, start_object/end_object, comma, key, string, number, and atom methods (true/false/null). Key design point: pretty printing can be added without duplicating the DOM traversal or escaping logic by parameterizing the output behavior behind the formatter interface — the traversal emits structural events, and only the formatter's open/close/comma/key hooks need to insert whitespace and indentation.

then access the parsed data using this in-memory model.
